gaps.name: In-chat search inside secret chats (catalogue bucket is wrong)
gaps.whatItIs: The modern client searches secret-chat history with searchSecretMessages, a purely local database search over decrypted messages, with an opaque string offset instead of a message-id cursor. searchChatMessages explicitly cannot be used in secret chats with a non-empty query, and searchMessages skips secret chats entirely.
gaps.whyItMatters: Without it, opening the search bar in a secret chat either silently returns nothing or returns a TDLib error, so a whole chat becomes unsearchable. The existing feature-catalogue entry 'Secret chat search' (area: search) is bucketed blocked with the rationale that this client does not implement E2E sessions -- that rationale is wrong: TDLib performs all the E2E work itself once use_secret_chats is YES, and searchSecretMessages hits only the local DB. The correct bucket is small.
gaps.whereItGoes: New wrapper in /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/iTgLegacy/src/TGClient+Search.h next to -searchMessagesInChat:, plus a branch in the in-chat search path of TGChatViewController.m that picks it when [[TGClient shared] isSecretChat:chatId]. The string-offset paging needs its own cursor field, it is not the fromMessageId model the other searches use.

gaps.name: Delete confirmation must not offer 'Delete for Me' in secret chats
gaps.whatItIs: In a secret chat every deletion is an E2E delete instruction sent to the peer; the modern client forces revoke and its clear-history flow uses a secret-chat-specific case (canClearForMyself = .secretChat in ChatControllerNavigationButtonAction.swift) rather than the normal for-me/for-everyone choice.
gaps.whyItMatters: TGChatViewController.m:5501 always builds an action sheet with both 'Delete for Everyone' and 'Delete for Me', and :3434/:3437 pass forEveryone NO or YES. In a secret chat the 'Delete for Me' branch is a lie: the message goes from the peer's device too. A privacy feature that misrepresents what deletion does is worse than not having it.
gaps.whereItGoes: The delete action sheet and selection-mode delete in /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/iTgLegacy/src/TGChatViewController.m (around lines 3434, 5501, 5527), gated on -isSecretChat: from TGClient+SecretChats.h. Same gate for the Clear History row in TGProfileViewController.m.

gaps.name: Forward / copy / save disabled for secret-chat content
gaps.whatItIs: The modern client treats every secret chat as copy-protected: ChatControllerOpenMessageContextMenu.swift computes isSecret from the peer namespace and drops Forward, Copy, Share and Save-to-gallery from the message context menu and from the media viewer; forwarding into a secret chat also force-hides sender names.
gaps.whyItMatters: Our message action sheet and forward picker are chat-type agnostic, so a user could forward a self-destructing photo out of the secret chat or copy its text into a cloud chat, defeating the point of the chat. TDLib will reject some of it, but only after the user has tapped, with an error they cannot interpret.
gaps.whereItGoes: The message long-press action sheet in /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/iTgLegacy/src/TGChatViewController.m and the media viewer's save/share buttons; -secretChat:allowsInputMessage: already exists for the inbound direction, this is the missing outbound half. Telegraph implements the same gating in TGSecretModernConversationCompanion.m, so the rules are readable there.

gaps.name: Self-destructing media viewer with countdown and auto-dismiss
gaps.whatItIs: Tapping secret media in the modern client opens a dedicated viewer that has no save/share chrome, draws a shrinking countdown while the TTL burns down, and dismisses itself and removes the bubble when it reaches zero. Telegraph has this as TGSecretPeerMediaGalleryModel / TGSecretInfiniteLifetimePeerMediaGalleryModel.
gaps.whyItMatters: The catalogue covers the blurred 'tap to view' bubble and openMessageContent, but not what happens after the tap. Without an auto-dismissing viewer, a one-view photo stays on screen indefinitely while the server-side timer expires behind it, which is exactly the failure mode secret media exists to prevent.
gaps.whereItGoes: A secret variant of the existing full-screen photo viewer in /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/iTgLegacy/src (the media viewer used by TGChatViewController), driven by -selfDestructInfoForMessage: 'remaining' and one shared NSTimer. Port from /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/twelve/Telegraph/TGSecretPeerMediaGalleryModel.m.

gaps.name: Handshake state as the chat-list row preview
gaps.whatItIs: The chat list in the modern client replaces the last-message preview of a secret chat with its handshake state text -- 'Waiting for X to accept the chat', 'X cancelled the chat', 'X joined your secret chat' -- rendered in the secret-chat accent colour, and only shows real message text once the chat is ready.
gaps.whyItMatters: Our wrapper exposes -secretChatStatusForChat:completion: but only the chat header is described as a consumer. A pending secret chat that shows a blank row in the chat list looks broken; the handshake can sit pending for days until the peer's device comes online, and that is precisely when the user needs to be told why nothing is happening.
gaps.whereItGoes: Cell configuration in /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/iTgLegacy/src/TGChatListViewController.m, alongside the lock glyph from the already-catalogued 'Secret-chat visual identity' entry, reading -secretChatInfoForChat:'s state field.

gaps.name: Restart a closed secret chat
gaps.whatItIs: When a secret chat is in the closed state, the modern client keeps the row but turns the composer into a 'Start a new secret chat' entry point that calls createNewSecretChat with the same user, since a closed chat can never be revived.
gaps.whyItMatters: closeSecretChat is wrapped and the catalogue covers closing, but nothing covers the state afterwards. A closed chat with a live-looking input bar that silently rejects every send is a dead end; the user has no way to learn they must create a fresh chat.
gaps.whereItGoes: The composer-disabled state in /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/iTgLegacy/src/TGChatViewController.m, driven by -canSendInSecretChat:completion: which already reports the state string; the button reuses -createSecretChatWithUser: from TGProfileViewController.m:1336.

gaps.name: Suppress message previews in notifications for secret chats
gaps.whatItIs: The modern client never puts secret-chat message text or media into a notification body; it shows only 'Encrypted message' plus the sender, and notificationTypeNewSecretChat gets its own wording.
gaps.whyItMatters: A self-destructing message whose text is echoed verbatim on the lock screen is not secret. Our notification path formats previews uniformly, so enabling secret chats without this gate actively leaks the content the feature is meant to protect.
gaps.whereItGoes: The notification text builder in /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/iTgLegacy/src/TGClient+Notifications.m and the local-notification path in AppDelegate.m; -textForSecretChatNotification: in TGClient+SecretChats.h already covers only the new-chat case.

gaps.name: Inline-bot warning in secret chats
gaps.whatItIs: Using an inline bot inside a secret chat sends the query to the bot's server, so the modern client shows a one-time alert (Conversation_SecretChatContextBotAlert) the first time it happens in a secret chat, remembered by a notice flag.
gaps.whyItMatters: It is the one place where a secret chat quietly stops being end-to-end, and the user has no other signal. Cheap to add and the only honest way to keep inline bots available in these chats.
gaps.whereItGoes: The inline-bot query path in /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/iTgLegacy/src/TGChatViewController.m, using TGAlertView plus an NSUserDefaults once-flag; alternatively suppress inline bots outright via -secretChat:allowsInputMessage:.

gaps.name: Terminate the secret chat when reporting or blocking the peer
gaps.whatItIs: ChatControllerReport.swift calls terminateSecretChat(requestRemoteHistoryRemoval: true) whenever the reported chat is a secret chat, so reporting also kills the session and wipes history on both devices.
gaps.whyItMatters: Reporting or blocking someone while an active E2E session with them stays alive is a real hole: the session keeps accepting their messages. It is one extra call on a path we already have.
gaps.whereItGoes: The Report / Block flows in /Users/alexanderhavrysh/Git/iOS/iTgLegacy/src/TGProfileViewController.m, calling the already-wrapped -closeSecretChatForChat:deleteHistory:.

gaps.name: Outgoing screenshot detection (confirming the blocked bucket)
gaps.whatItIs: The modern client reports screenshots taken over a secret chat so the peer sees 'X took a screenshot!'.
gaps.whyItMatters: Reported only to close it out: this is genuinely blocked and the catalogue is right. UIApplicationUserDidTakeScreenshotNotification is iOS 7+ and Telegraph's own TGScreenCaptureSignals.m returns an empty signal for iosMajorVersion() < 7, so even the reference Objective-C fork has no pre-iOS-7 path. Separately, this TDLib schema (tdlib/td/td/generate/scheme/td_api.tl) has no sendChatScreenshotTakenNotification function at all -- only the messageScreenshotTaken content type -- so the inbound service row is achievable and the outbound half is not, on two independent grounds.
gaps.whereItGoes: Nowhere. The inbound 'X took a screenshot!' service row already has its wrapper in -secretServiceTextForMessage: and belongs in the TGChatViewController.m service-row formatter.
tdlib: messageScreenshotTaken (inbound only; no send-side method exists in this schema)
